item.title: [7] Thermal Phase Transition of Three Dimensional Orthogonal Metals
item.description:
Last authors: Hanbit Oh, Eun-Gook Moon

Authors: Inho Song, Minsu Park, Hanbit Oh, Eun-Gook Moon

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Electronic structure theory and ARPES spectral signatures for a class of correlated metals.

Tags: #ARPES #correlated #theory

Abstract: Orthogonal metals provide a paradigmatic example of strongly entangled metallic states whose transport and thermodynamic properties resemble those of conventional Fermi liquids, while their single-electron excitations remain fundamentally distinct. Despite considerable interest in their unusual ground-state properties, orthogonal metals in three spatial dimensions and their finite-temperature behavior remain relatively unexplored. Here, we investigate a three-dimensional orthogonal metal and characterize the thermodynamic and spectroscopic signatures associated with its finite-temperature phase transition. Starting from a simple model of fermions coupled to spin degrees of freedom, we perturbatively demonstrate that the thermal transition known to occur in the purely bosonic limit persists in the presence of coupling to a gapless Fermi surface. We then examine physical observables that change prominently between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes. In particular, we calculate the evolution of the physical-electron spectral function and identify characteristic signatures in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. We find a pronounced contrast in low-energy spectral weight between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes without requiring conventional symmetry-breaking order. Our results establish finite-temperature orthogonal-metal physics as a possible mechanism for pseudogap-like behavior in three-dimensional and quasi-two-dimensional layered materials with non-negligible interlayer hopping, which may be applied to the recent experiments in $\mathrm{Sr_2 VO_3 Fe As}$.

item.title: [7] Collective Modes of Fractional States Beyond Landau Levels
item.description:
Last authors: Peleg Emanuel, Yuval Oreg

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant study on collective modes in fractional topological matter.

Tags: #topological #fractional #theory

Abstract: Collective modes provide a powerful probe into the properties and stability of topologically ordered and strongly interacting phases of matter, such as fractional quantum Hall states. Yet, the description of fractional-state excitations away from the Landau-level limit remains a formidable challenge. We develop a framework for describing collective excitations in the strong-coupling regime of coupled-wire constructions and show that they emerge as solitons and breathers of effective sine-Gordon theories. This approach provides a systematic route to studying collective modes in a broad class of fractional states. Applied to a coupled-wire construction of the fractional quantum Hall effect, the framework captures key features of the magnetoroton branch. It naturally extends to fractional Chern insulators, demonstrating that magnetoroton-like collective modes persist well beyond the Landau-level limit. We find that the magnetoroton gap increases as the Fubini-Study metric approaches the ideal (trace-condition) limit, highlighting the important role of quantum geometry in the stability of fractionalized phases and their collective excitations. The same trend favors the stability of the long-wavelength quadrupolar mode associated with the chiral graviton. Together, these results identify a distinct interplay between fractionalization and quantum geometry, and provide an analytical framework for studies of collective excitations in fractional topological matter.

item.title: [9] Coexisting Kondo and Weyl-like transport in kagome heavy-fermion metal, YbyCo3Ge3-xSnx
item.description:
Last authors: M. E. Kamminga, S. Wiedmann, J. Y. Chan, M. N. Ali

Authors: M. P. Dubbelman, R. Meduri, T. M. Kyrk, Z. Cheng, P. Maderson, D. Pizzirani, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct relevance to kagome metals, topology, and ARPES/spectroscopy in correlated systems.

Tags: #kagome #ARPES #Weyl #correlated

Abstract: Strong electron correlations and topology offer complementary routes to controlling electrical conduction, as correlations can make electrons heavy (e.g. Kondo lattices) whereas topology can make them behave as massless particles (e.g. Dirac or Weyl systems), and having both in one material is rare. In Kondo lattice systems, Kondo hybridization between localized 4$f$ and conduction electrons strongly enhances the quasiparticle mass, where in Weyl-Kondo systems these Kondo-renormalized bands form Weyl states, and simultaneous signs of both Kondo and Weyl states in one material have not been observed in transport. Here we report signs of both in the kagome metal \ce{Yb_yCo3Ge_{3-x}Sn_x} by combining magnetotransport, heat capacity, magnetization, angle-resolved and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy, and DFT+U calculations to reveal Yb-dependent Kondo scattering developing into lattice coherence, with extrapolated Sommerfeld coefficient of approximately 2 ~Jmol$_{\mathrm{Yb}}^{-1}$K$^{-2}$. Transverse magnetoresistance (MR) follows single-ion Kondo scaling, whereas longitudinal transport contains an additional negative response proportional to B$^2$ and remains unsaturated up to 32 T, consistent with a chiral anomaly. These findings support a picture of Kondo and Weyl-like conduction arising from distinct electronic states without external Fermi-level tuning, suggesting a possible route to combining correlated and topological functionality in a bulk material.

item.title: [8] Repulsion-Driven Topological Superconductivity in Twisted MoTe2
item.description:
Last authors: Taige Wang, Daniel E. Parker

Authors: Tianle Wang, Tomohiro Soejima, Norman Y. Yao, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Topological superconductivity in moire systems with direct relevance to current research.

Tags: #moire #superconductivity #topological

Abstract: We show that a microscopic model of twisted MoTe$_2$ with screened Coulomb interactions produces topological superconductivity. Using the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) on infinite cylinders, we find that the narrow Chern band of twisted MoTe$_2$ has Cooper pair correlations that strengthen with cylinder circumference, consistent with two dimensional superconductivity. The superconductor has chiral $f$-wave pairing around the valley center, and its topology produces chiral Majorana edge modes and non-Abelian vortex cores. At zero displacement field, the superconductor spans fillings $-0.78\lesssim\nu\lesssim-0.72$, close to the experimental range, and extends in a dome to finite displacement field. We then predict how its stiffness evolves with the filling and the tunable displacement field. The interplay with screening length is also examined. Nearby, we find a fractional Chern insulator, a topological charge density wave, a metal, and a charge-ordered state. The last is a candidate for the reentrant integer Hall regime in experiments. These results establish a route from repulsive interactions in microscopic models of moir\'e materials to chiral topological uperconductors with chiral Majorana edge modes.

item.title: [8] Possibility of Potts Spin-Ice in Rare Earth Twisted-Kagome Layers: an Example of DyAgGe
item.description:
Last authors: Hari Bhandari, Nirmal J. Ghimire

Authors: Gunnar F. Schwertfeger, Po-Hao Chang, Predrag Nikolic, Igor I. Mazin, Hari Bhandari, Nirmal J. Ghimire

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant kagome-based magnetic material study.

Tags: #kagome #magnetic

Abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) spin-ice compounds, predominantly based on the pyrochlore or spinel structure, have been attracting considerable interest in the last two decades. A two-dimensional (2D) analogue is the spin-ice consisting of kagome planes. So far, only Ising spin ice has been discovered in any material, and only one 2D material, the kagome compound HoAgGe, has been identified as a spin ice. In this Letter, we show that another rare-earth twisted Kagome magnetic compound, DyAgGe, is in fact a Potts spin ice (or color ice), where at each site not two but four spin directions are allowed. We argue that an 8-state spin ice may also exist in this class of systems. We present a first-principles calculation of magnetic interactions in DyAgGe, and confirm the 4-state Potts structure of this material by matching our model predictions with the available experimental data.

item.title: [9] Constraining the Superconducting Gap of Monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3 via Statistical Analysis and Tip-Height-Dependent Tunneling Spectroscopy
item.description:
Last authors: Hanno H. Weitering, Wonhee Ko

Authors: Dongwon Shin, Xiyou Peng, Kaleb McClure, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Directly relevant STM/STS studies on high-Tc iron-based superconductor monolayers.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #STM #superconductivity #FeSe

Abstract: Monolayer FeSe grown on SrTiO$_3$ (001) exemplifies interface-enhanced superconductivity, exhibiting a transition temperature nearly ten times that of bulk FeSe. Yet, its tunneling spectra lack clearly identifiable superconducting coherence peaks, preventing an unambiguous determination of the gap magnitude. Here, we use ultralow-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy as a function of temperature, tip-sample separation, and lateral position to disentangle tunneling contributions by statistical analysis. Decay rates extracted by regression of tip-height-dependent spectroscopy reveal three energy regimes: Andreev-reflection-dominated tunneling below 6 meV, mixed Andreev and quasiparticle tunneling between 6 and 13 meV, and predominantly quasiparticle tunneling above 13 meV. Spatially resolved spectroscopy and correlation analysis further reveal that the tunneling conductance is predominantly localized near defects below 6 meV but becomes spatially extended at higher energies. Together, these results constrain the superconducting gap to lie between 6 and 13 meV. Our findings establish statistical analysis of spectroscopy as a powerful approach to constraining superconducting gap structures when complex spectral features prevent the unambiguous identification of coherence peaks.

item.title: [7] Korringa factor in Dirac-nodal-line systems
item.description:
Last authors: Takahiko Sekine, Kanoda Kazushi

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important theoretical interpretation for NMR in topological semimetals/Dirac systems.

Tags: #Dirac #topological

Abstract: The Korringa factor $K(\alpha)$ in the nuclear magnetic resonance studies is a widely used measure of electron-correlation effects in metals and is conventionally interpreted using the non-correlated value $K(\alpha)$ = 1. In Dirac-fermion systems, however, the non-correlated reference value depends on the electronic density of states (DOS) and differs from that of conventional metals. Here, we theoretically investigate the non-correlated Korringa factor $K^*(\alpha)$ in a Dirac nodal-line (DNL) system with finite nodal-line dispersion using a DOS-based approach. We show that $K^*(\alpha)$ exhibits an intrinsic temperature dependence, continuously evolving from the Dirac-fermion value of 1.71 at high temperatures to the metallic value of 1 at low temperatures. The crossover temperature is found to be proportional to the nodal-line dispersion width, identified as the characteristic energy scale governing the non-correlated Korringa factor in DNL systems. We further demonstrate that Landau quantization generates singular DOS structures that strongly enhance $K^*(\alpha)$, producing pronounced peaks even in the absence of electron correlations. In addition, $K^*(\alpha)$ exhibits two distinct types of magnetic oscillations arising from intra-level and inter-level contributions. The latter originates from the overlap of singular points belonging to positive and negative quantum-number Landau subbands at the Fermi level and represents a unique consequence of the finite energy dispersion of a DNL. These results provide a quantitative reference for interpreting NMR experiments in DNL materials and for identifying genuine correlation effects beyond DOS-induced contributions.

item.title: [10] Dynamical Phonon Anharmonicity Drives Charge-Density-Wave Softening and Electronic Quasiparticle Decoherence in Monolayer 1H-NbSe2
item.description:
Last authors: Yi Xia

Score 10/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Extremely relevant to CDW studies in 2D materials, with direct connection to electronic structure.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #CDW #NbSe2 #monolayer #electronicstructure

Abstract: Charge-density-wave (CDW) instabilities in two-dimensional materials are governed by strongly anharmonic soft phonons, whose dynamical behavior remains poorly understood beyond the statically renormalized vibrations. Here, using monolayer 1H-NbSe2, we investigate how frequency-dependent three- and four-phonon interactions reshape phonon spectral functions and influence electronic excitations. We find that three-phonon interactions induce substantial dynamical softening of CDW modes, increasing the estimated transition temperature relative to static self-consistent phonon theory. Four-phonon interactions further promote such dynamical softening and enhance spectral broadening, producing non-Lorentzian lineshapes that challenge the quasiparticle picture. Incorporating dynamically renormalized phonon frequencies and electron-phonon coupling into Fan-Migdal electron self-energy calculations reveals enhanced electronic kinks, satellite features, and momentum-dependent quasiparticle decoherence, driven by the strong momentum dependence of the electron-phonon coupling matrix elements. These findings establish dynamical anharmonicity as a critical link between soft-mode lattice fluctuations and electronic spectral signatures, providing insights into coupled lattice-electron dynamics in two-dimensional quantum materials.

item.title: [7] Resolving magnetic order and dynamics with polarized neutron scattering: a practical guide to longitudinal polarization analysis
item.description:
Last authors: Sijie Xu, Pengcheng Dai

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Practical guide for neutron scattering on magnetic orders including kagome magnets and altermagnets.

Tags: #method #kagome #altermagnetism

Abstract: Neutron scattering provides microscopic information on magnetic order and spin dynamics. Most experiments, however, use unpolarized neutrons and do not fully exploit the information carried by the neutron spin. Longitudinal polarization analysis (LPA), established in the pioneering work of Moon, Riste, and Koehler at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in the late 1960s, separates magnetic and nonmagnetic scattering contributions through their different effects on the neutron spin. In this review, we illustrate how LPA can distinguish weak magnetic scattering from nonmagnetic contributions, constrain small moment components, and resolve the spin-space anisotropy of magnetic excitations. We introduce the formalism connecting measured polarization channels to magnetic quantities and discuss scattering geometry, crystallographic projections, and corrections for finite polarization. Our aim is to provide a practical guide for neutron scatterers using LPA to determine magnetic structures and characterize spin excitations in quantum materials. We conclude with opportunities in altermagnets, unconventional superconductors, and kagome magnets.

item.title: [7] Thermally enhanced magnon-phonon resonance in van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3
item.description:
Last authors: Qingming Zhang, Je-Geun Park

Authors: Kai-Xuan Zhang, Beom Hyun Kim, Seungbok Lee, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of magnon-phonon coupling in a relevant van der Waals antiferromagnet.

Tags: #experiment #material #vanderWaals

Abstract: Strong coupling between collective excitations provides a route to controlling quantum states of matter, yet its evolution under thermal fluctuations remains poorly understood. In the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3, strong magnon-phonon coupling is established at low temperatures. At the same time, recent terahertz experiments revealed the counterintuitive stabilization of a long-lived metastable magnetic state with an exceedingly long lifetime of 5 msec at the antiferromagnetic transition, not at the base temperature. This was attributed to a strongly coupled spin-lattice scenario, challenging the conventional wisdom that increased magnetic and thermal fluctuations near TN should be detrimental to the coherent control of a metastable phase. Thus it requires an independent examination for correct understanding. Using high-field Raman spectroscopy, we systematically investigate the temperature evolution of magnon-phonon coupling in FePS3. We observe a pronounced avoided crossing between magnon and phonon modes across a wide range of temperatures and find that the coupling strength remains remarkably robust with increasing temperatures. The zero-field magnon-phonon detuning decreases progressively with warming, driving the system toward resonance and thereby enhancing their hybridization near the transition temperature. This anomalous thermal evolution provides the crucial key to understanding the unusual terahertz-driven states recently reported in FePS3. More broadly, our results highlight van der Waals magnets as a promising platform for strong coupling among collective excitations and for controlling magnetic states through light-matter interactions.

Abstract: Nonrelativistic spin splitting in collinear compensated magnets is constrained by spin-group symmetry, with distinct alternating and Zeeman-type splitting typically associated with altermagnets and fully compensated ferrimagnets, respectively. These results connect the spatial organization of spin density with the electronic response to structural inequivalence, providing a design principle for hybrid spin splitting in compensated magnets.

Abstract: We investigate the effects of ionic hydrogen (H$^+$) intake on the occupied and unoccupied states of MnSb$_2$Te$_4$, a van der Waals magnetic material. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and time-resolved ARPES, combined with resonant and core level photoemission, we reveal that hydrogen binds near specific lattice sites, locally redistributing charge density and reshaping the valence band spectral weight. Abstract: The predominantly $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave pairing symmetry of cuprate superconductors is well established, yet its microscopic manifestation in local Cooper-pair tunneling remains less explored. Here, we investigate Bi$_{1.2}$Pb$_{0.8}$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+\delta}$, using Josephson scanning tunneling spectroscopy with a conventional $s$-wave superconducting Pb tip. We observe a zero-bias conductance enhancement whose approximately quadratic dependence on junction conductance is consistent with phase-diffusive Josephson tunneling. Atomic-resolution conductance maps and site-resolved spectra reveal a pronounced intra-unit-cell modulation, with enhanced Josephson response near oxygen sites and strong suppression near copper sites and along diagonal directions. Microscopic calculations incorporating the bilayer electronic structure and realistic Wannier-based tunneling matrix elements reproduce the observed spatial pattern through interference between pairing contributions of opposite signs. Our results reveal how the sign-changing $d$-wave superconducting order parameter manifests itself in atomic-scale Josephson tunneling, providing complementary evidence for unconventional pairing symmetry in cuprates.

Abstract: The absence of magnetic Bragg peaks and a broad excitation continuum are commonly recognized experimental features of a quantum spin liquid. The Ce-based triangular-lattice hexaaluminate CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$ exhibits both signatures, yet its effective model and ground state remain under debate. Experiments have variously suggested a quantum spin liquid, proximate umbrella point, and disorder-suppressed magnetic order. Here we trace these contradictions to an overlooked multipolar degree of freedom: the transverse pseudospin of the $|\pm5/2\rangle$ Kramers doublet is a rank-5 triakontadipole rather than an ordinary dipole. Analyzing the magnetization, neutron spectra, and thermodynamics on equal footing, we establish a dipole-triakontadipole XXZ model with $J_{\perp} \simeq 0.65$ K and $J_c \simeq -0.13$ K. The resulting planar triakontadipolar superfluid order is hidden from dipolar probes, explaining the absence of a magnetic Bragg peak in neutron scattering. The zero-field excitations separate into a low-energy triakontadipole wave and a broad higher-energy continuum. We further propose nuclear spin-lattice relaxation and spin-current experiments to probe the gapless excitations of this hidden triakontadipole superfluid. Our findings thus open a new avenue for high-rank multipolar physics in rare-earth triangular-lattice magnets.

Why: Experimental control of spin transport in a correlated oxide heterostructure ($VO_2$).

item.title: [7] Symmetry-protected isolation of the quantum metric in chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals
item.description:
Last authors: Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of topological semi-metals with clear experimental transport signatures.

Tags: #theory #Dirac #topological

Abstract: Quantum geometry, comprising the Berry curvature (BC) and the quantum metric (QM), underpins a wide array of topological and transport phenomena. However, in most solid-state platforms, BC and QM signals are inherently entangled, making their experimental separation highly challenging. Here, we demonstrate that the chiral limit of type-II semi-Dirac semimetals provides a symmetry-protected mechanism to cleanly isolate the QM. At the chiral limit where the spin-orbit gap $m_z=0$, chiral and $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetries strictly suppress the BC, its dipole (BCD), and the shift current, leaving the QM and its dipole (QMD) as the sole sources of the optical and nonlinear Hall responses. This pure-QM regime exhibits distinct experimental fingerprints, including a divergent longitudinal optical conductivity and a QMD-induced nonlinear Hall conductivity that exhibits a pronounced singularity as the chemical potential approaches the nodal point. Turning on a finite $m_z$ reactivates the BC channels, transitioning the system from a pure-QM phase into a mixed geometric phase. By deriving a scaling law for the nonlinear Hall conductivity, we establish a direct experimental strategy to separate the mixed Drude, BCD, and QMD contributions based on their distinct relaxation-time dependencies. Our findings identify chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals as highly tunable platforms for isolating and probing intrinsic quantum geometric effects.

item.title: [7] Vortices in a two-dimensional fermionic superfluid
item.description:
Last authors: Cesar Raymundo Cabrera, Henning Moritz

Authors: Artak Mkrtchyan, Hans Leonard Michel, Moritz von Usslar, Ren\'e Henke, Cesar Raymundo Cabrera, Henning Moritz

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of 2D fermionic superfluidity and BKT physics.

Tags: #experiment #superconduct #transport

Abstract: Quantized vortices are a hallmark of superfluidity. They have proven to be an indispensable probe for systems ranging from superfluid helium to type-II superconductors. In ultracold two-dimensional (2D) Fermi gases, where phase fluctuations are enhanced and the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) mechanism governs the superfluid transition, their observation has remained elusive. Here, we report on the controlled creation of quantized vortices in a homogeneous 2D gas in the BEC--BCS crossover. By continuously tuning the velocity of two moving obstacles, we observe quantized steps in the absolute vortex charge. Matter-wave interferometry reveals the characteristic phase winding, quantized in units of $2\pi$. Measurements on 2D and 3D gases show a striking difference: only in 2D does the vortex number grow with temperature, reflecting thermal activation of BKT vortex pairs. Our approach provides evidence of fermionic superfluidity in 2D and offers a means to study BKT physics, vortex-controlled transport and resistance, as well as to detect unconventional superfluidity in spin-imbalanced 2D gases.

item.title: [8] Twisting the pseudo-magnetic field lattice in periodically strained Graphene
item.description:
Last authors: C. B. Winkelmann, M. Zelzmann, G. Trambly de Laissardi\`ere, V. T. Renard

Authors: L-M. Benneka, T. Rhouma, C. B. Winkelmann, M. Zelzmann, G. Trambly de Laissardi\`ere, V. T. Renard

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important study on strain engineering in graphene with correlations.

Tags: #material #graphene #correlated

Abstract: Periodic deformations flatten electronic bands of graphene which could host strongly correlated electrons similar to those observed in twisted graphene bilayers. The most spectacular effects of strong correlations like superconductivity or magnetism have however not yet been observed despite several experimental attempts. Here, we use tight-binding calculations to investigate the effect of twisting the periodic strain lattice with respect to the atomic lattice. item.title: [9] Evidence for a Dirac Spin Liquid in the Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet from High-Precision Neural-Network Quantum States
item.description:
Last authors: Ao Chen, Markus Heyl

Authors: Zheng-Hang Sun, Christopher Roth, Ao Chen, Markus Heyl

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Crucial study on kagome magnetism and potential spin liquid ground states.

Tags: #material #kagome #theory

Abstract: The spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet is a central model in the study of quantum spin liquids, yet its ground-state properties remain unresolved. We perform large-scale variational Monte-Carlo calculations using neural-network quantum states (NQSs) with kagome-geometry-aware message-passing convolution on two-dimensional tori containing up to 300 spins, and achieve exceptionally low variational energies for the kagome model. The spin and dimer structure factors show no evidence of magnetic or valence-bond long-range order. Finally, the fidelity of the optimized NQSs with Gutzwiller-projected mean-field states increasingly favors the Dirac state over the competing $Z_{2}$ candidates as the system size grows. Together, these complementary results provide evidence for a $U(1)$ Dirac spin-liquid ground state in the kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet.

item.title: [7] Exact Rokhsar-Kivelson points hosting first-order phase transitions in S=1 compass models
item.description:
Last authors: Jay Pandey

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of kagome models relevant to spin liquids.

Tags: #kagome #theory

Abstract: We study $S=1$ compass models on the square and kagome lattices with bond-dependent bilinear and biquadratic interactions parametrized by an angle $\theta$. For compatible geometries, we determine the exact ground-state manifolds throughout the interval $\pi/4\leq\theta\leq3\pi/4$. At each endpoint, a product of on-site unitaries maps the Hamiltonian to the Laplacian of a configuration graph $\mathcal{G}$ in the $S=1$ Cartesian basis. These endpoints are exact Rokhsar-Kivelson (RK) points, with one ground state per dynamically connected component of $\mathcal{G}$. Each such state is an equal-amplitude superposition in the transformed basis and acquires configuration-dependent phases upon transforming back to the original basis. Both models possess $m=O(L)$ independent and mutually commuting conserved $\mathbb{Z}_2$ line charges, where $L$ is the linear system size, forcing a ground-state degeneracy of at least $2^m$ at the RK endpoints. Throughout the interior region, $\pi/4<\theta<3\pi/4$, the ground-state manifold on each lattice is instead spanned by two product states, both annihilated by the Hamiltonian. On both lattices, each RK endpoint also hosts a first-order transition into this intervening interior phase spanned by the two product states with long-range order.

item.description:
Last authors: Zhen Huang, Lin Lin

Authors: Hao-En Li, Zhen Huang, Lin Lin

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Highly relevant method for modeling correlated impurities and transport; mentions STM.

Abstract: Quantum impurity calculations become challenging when multiple correlated orbitals are treated explicitly, particularly in nonequilibrium steady states. We introduce Coupled-Cluster Coupled Lindblad (C$^3$L), a deterministic approach that combines the recently developed coupled-Lindblad compact bath representation with coupled-cluster theory to compute steady states and Green's functions directly in imaginary and real frequency. C$^3$L has favorable polynomial computational complexity and avoids the sign problem of quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). In a real-time multiorbital benchmark, it agrees closely with state-of-the-art QMC while reducing computational cost by four to five orders of magnitude, with a further 10--100-fold speedup on a GPU. Beyond the practical reach of established real-time QMC solvers, four-orbital nonequilibrium impurities with general interactions and biased reservoirs become accessible with C$^3$L. We obtain resonance-resolved transport signatures relevant to scanning tunneling microscopy experiments on molecular junctions.

Abstract: Chiral two-dimensional electron gases, which capture the electronic properties of graphene and rhombohedral graphene systems, exhibit singular momentum-space vortices and are susceptible to interaction-induced topological Haldane phases. Abstract: Ab initio calculations and angle-resolved photoemission experiments demonstrate that the bulk and surface electronic structure of Weyl semimetal candidate MoTe2 changes significantly by tuning the chemical potential by less than 0.4 eV. Calculations indicate that several Lifshitz transitions can occur among multiple electron and hole Fermi pockets of differing orbital character. Deposition of alkali atoms on the surface produces electron binding energy shifts consistent with increased band filling. The results indicate that multiple regimes of electronic properties can be easily accessed in this versatile, layered material.

item.title: [8] Spectroscopic Evidence of Competing Diagonal Spin Interactions and Spin Disproportionation in the Bilayer Nickelate La3Ni2O7
item.description:
Last authors: Meng Wang, Kee Hoon Kim

Authors: Dong-Hyeon Gim, Dirk Wulferding, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Meng Wang, Kee Hoon Kim

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Spectroscopic study of electronic/magnetic excitations in high-Tc relevant nickelates.

Tags: #nickelate #superconductivity #spectroscopy #magnons

Abstract: A comprehensive spectroscopic map of the electronic, magnetic, and lattice excitations is presented for the bilayer nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ using Raman scattering at ambient pressure. Upon entering the spin density wave state below 153 K, the $A_{1g}$ channel exhibits an abrupt electronic spectral gap with a clear isosbestic point. In contrast, the $B_{1g}$ and $B_{2g}$ channels are dominated by pronounced two-magnon (2M) excitations, representing a signature of incipient Mottness. These 2M signals in both channels constitute evidence for two distinct in-plane spin exchange interactions along the Ni-O bonding and its diagonal directions. Calculations based on the spin wave theory further reveal that the 2M mode in the $B_{2g}$ channel arises from the competition between two bond-diagonal antiferromagnetic interactions mediated by nickel $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals. Furthermore, emergent low-energy 2M excitations below 10 meV are found to originate from distinct, weaker spin moments, supporting spin disproportionation. Simultaneously, an anomalous softening of $B_{1g}$ phonons from 280 down to 4.5 K is uncovered, suggesting the presence of an incipient lattice instability leading to checkerboard-type breathing modulations. Collectively, these findings identify a ground state of the bilayer nickelate characterized by competing bond-diagonal interactions, spin disproportionation, and an incipient lattice instability, establishing key ingredients for understanding the mechanism of nickelate superconductivity.

item.title: [7] Collective phase modes in twisted d-wave superconducting bilayers
item.description:
Last authors: Miao Liu, Sheng Meng

Authors: Yin Shi, Mengxian Zhao, Fei Yang, Miao Liu, Sheng Meng

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of superconducting phase fluctuations relevant to twisted van der Waals systems.

Tags: #superconductivity #twistedbilayers #cuprates

Abstract: Twisted cuprate bilayers have been predicted to host high-temperature chiral $d+id'$ superconductivity, originating from higher-order Josephson coupling processes. In such two-dimensional superconducting systems, long-wavelength fluctuations in the phase of the superconducting order parameter constitute gapless collective modes and therefore remain significant even at zero temperature. Here, we perform a theoretical analysis of the low-energy phase fluctuations in twisted $d$-wave superconducting bilayers within a self-consistent harmonic approximation, systematically retaining Josephson coupling to all orders. We demonstrate that higher-order Josephson coupling processes lead to nontrivial modifications of the phase dynamics. The momentum-resolved summand of the relative-phase stiffness is nonzero even in the normal state because interlayer tunneling explicitly breaks the intralayer U(1) symmetry, but its momentum integral vanishes for the continuum dispersion. The relative-phase stiffness is smaller in the $d+id'$ phase than in the $d$-wave phase, while the overall-phase stiffness has the opposite behavior. Furthermore, phase fluctuations strongly soften the Josephson plasma frequency near a twist angle of $45^\circ$ and also substantially reduce the Josephson critical current.

item.title: [7] Chiral Phonons Coupled to Spin-Split Bands in Altermagnetic CrSb and MnTe
item.description:
Last authors: Giancarlo Panaccione, Domenico Di Sante

Authors: Armando Consiglio, Maximilian \"Unzelmann, Giancarlo Panaccione, Domenico Di Sante

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Altermagnetism and chiral phonon-electronic coupling, specifically relevant to future ARPES experiments.

Tags: #altermagnet #phonon #photoemission

Abstract: Altermagnets exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization, providing a unique platform where magnetic order, electronic structure and lattice dynamics intertwine. Here, using first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that the prototypical altermagnets CrSb and MnTe host locally chiral phonon modes carrying finite phonon angular momentum with a six-lobes $f$-wave texture in momentum space. Our results show that the chiral lattice motion originates from the pnictogen/chalcogen sublattice, while the altermagnetic spin splitting is generated by the magnetic transition-metal atoms, indicating that chiral lattice dynamics and altermagnetic electronic states originate from different atomic sublattices of the same crystal. In pristine compounds, at each valley, inversion symmetry suppresses the net phonon angular momentum despite local circular atomic motion. We further demonstrate that isoelectronic symmetry lowering induced by chemical substitution lifts this cancellation and generates finite valley phonon chirality, while keeping the altermagnetic nature of the compounds intact. Most importantly, we reveal that chiral phonons couple to momentum-dependent spin-split electronic bands through momentum-dependent electron-phonon interaction, producing characteristic modifications of the electronic structure, possibly accessible by photoemission experiments. Our results establish altermagnets as a promising platform for chiral phononics and spin-selective lattice control.

item.title: [7] Magnetic ground states of CrPS4 and NiPS3 monolayers from long-range exchange interactions
item.description:
Last authors: Amador Garcia-Fuente, Jaime Ferrer

Authors: Balazs Nagyfalusi, Ritesh Das, Alvaro Bermejillo-Seco, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Predictive magnetism in 2D van der Waals materials, relevant to the broader quantum materials landscape.

Tags: #vanderWaals #magnetism #monolayer

Abstract: We investigate the magnetic properties of monolayer CrPS$_4$ and NiPS$_3$ by combining first-principles calculations, second-principles spin models, and Monte Carlo simulations. Unlike conventional approaches that truncate exchange interactions after only a few shells and determine them by fitting total energies, we extract the magnetic exchange tensors directly from density functional theory using the LKAG formalism and include interactions until numerical convergence is achieved. We show that long-range exchange interactions qualitatively modify the magnetic behavior of both materials. In CrPS$_4$, they destabilize the previously predicted ferromagnetic ground state and stabilize a spin-spiral phase, reducing the critical temperature to about 21\,K, in agreement with available experiments. The resulting magnetic phase diagram contains multiple collinear and non-collinear phases that can be tuned by temperature and external magnetic fields. In NiPS$_3$, the experimentally observed zigzag antiferromagnetic order only emerges when exchange interactions up to the fifth shell are included. These results demonstrate that quantitatively predictive spin models for thiophosphate monolayers require long-range exchange interactions and provide a predictive framework for accurately describing two-dimensional van der Waals magnets.

item.title: [9] Theory of Kondo hybridization wave in Kondo lattice
item.description:
Last authors: Yin Zhong

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Directly addresses spectroscopic features in heavy-fermion materials like UTe2 and TaS2 relevant to STM/electronic structure.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #Kondo-lattice #STM #heavy-fermions

Abstract: Recent scanning tunneling microscopy experiments have discovered emergent spatially modulated Kondo hybridization wave (KHW) order in the heavy fermion superconductor UTe$_2$ and the artificial Kondo lattice system 1T/1H-TaS$_2$, challenging the conventional paradigm of spatially uniform Kondo hybridization in heavy fermion physics. Here, we develop a microscopic theory for KHW order based on the canonical square-lattice Kondo lattice model within the large-$N$ fermionic mean-field approximation. We systematically identify stable modulated KHW phases and establish their ground-state phase diagram. The prominent $\boldsymbol{Q}=(0,\pi)$ KHW phase yields uniaxial stripe modulation of the Kondo hybridization gap, which faithfully reproduces the spatial modulation pattern observed in UTe$_2$. Moreover, its inherent unit-cell-doubling modulation precisely accounts for the spectroscopic features measured in 1T/1H-TaS$_2$. We further predict a characteristic in-plane conductivity anisotropy that serves as a definitive transport fingerprint to discriminate KHW states with distinct ordering wavevectors. Our work provides a microscopic foundation for the newly observed KHW order and establishes a unified theoretical framework for understanding emergent modulated hybridization phenomena in heavy fermion materials.

item.title: [8] Heavy-fermion hybridization waves from Dirac spinons near a Kondo-breakdown quantum phase transition
item.description:
Last authors: Matthias Vojta, Onur Erten

Authors: Pedro M. C\^onsoli, Matthias Vojta, Onur Erten

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relates emergent hybridization waves to electronic band structures and Dirac spinons in heavy-fermion systems.

Tags: #heavy-fermions #Dirac-spinons #electronic-structure

Abstract: Motivated by the recent observation of spatially modulated screening in different paramagnetic heavy-fermion materials, we propose a theoretical mechanism for the emergence of such hybridization waves in frustrated Kondo lattices with no magnetic order. By applying both a parton mean-field theory and a perturbative calculation to a minimal Kondo-Heisenberg lattice model, we demonstrate that a heavy Fermi liquid can naturally develop hybridization waves when it approaches a quantum phase transition where Kondo screening breaks down and the local magnetic moments form a Dirac spin liquid. We relate the strength of this mechanism to a kinematic condition on the electronic and spinon band structures and show that the spatial periodicity of the ensuing hybridization wave is controlled by momenta $\vec{Q}$ that connect the Dirac nodes in the spinon dispersion to low-energy portions of the electronic band structure.

item.title: [7] Chiral Superconductivity Adjacent to a Wigner Crystal in Rhombohedral Graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Ke Wang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Discusses unconventional chiral superconductivity in graphene, a topic of broader interest to the user.

Tags: #graphene #superconductivity #correlations

Abstract: It was experimentally observed that Wigner-crystal and chiral superconducting phases occur adjacent to each other in rhombohedral graphene. In this Letter, we explore electronic correlations underlying the two phases and identify the pairing mechanism of chiral superconductivity. Exchange correlations play an essential role in both phases. First, we use self-consistent Hartree-Fock calculations to identify a Wigner-crystal state. Second, to investigate the pairing mechanism, we go beyond charge screening and construct a particle-hole-renormalized interaction through the coupled parquet and Bethe-Salpeter equations. This interaction incorporates exchange correlations while preserving crossing symmetry. Within this framework, we find that electronic correlations in the quarter metal are strongly enhanced near the crystal phase boundary, generating an effective attraction that favors superconducting pairing. Consequently, chiral superconductivity (CSC) emerges in a narrow sliver adjacent to the crystal. Furthermore, we identify the winding number of the superconducting order parameter as $-3$, indicating its $f$-wave nature. These results connect the emergence of chiral pairing and its location in the phase diagram to the electronic correlations favoring crystallization.

item.title: [9] Optimised growth of epitaxial D019 Mn3Ge(0001) thin films via single target sputtering
item.description:
Last authors: Gavin Burnell, B J Hickey

Authors: Servet Ozdemir, Ping-Luen Ho, Callum Brennan-Rich, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Material-specific study of a kagome Weyl semimetal with giant anomalous Hall effect.

Tags: #kagome #Weyl-semimetal #Mn3Ge

Abstract: Materials with chemical identity Mn3X, where X is Sn, Ga, or Ge, are Heusler alloys with intriguing properties that are fundamentally and technologically interesting. They have topological properties with a non-trivial band structure that identify them as Weyl semimetals in the bulk. Their magnetic properties, which give rise to the topological band structure through spin-orbit coupling, are determined by their Kagome lattice structure, making them chiral non-collinear antiferromagnets. Among these materials, Mn3Ge is particularly interesting because it has a larger Berry curvature, leading to a large anomalous Hall conductivity and motivating potential spintronic applications. The desirable properties are only obtained when Mn3Ge has the D019 crystal structure, so producing an easily reproducible growth recipe is the main objective of this paper. Here we show that ultra-high-quality thin films of Mn3Ge with D019 symmetry can be grown from a Mn5Ge target on an Al2O3(0001) substrate with a Ru(0001) seed layer. The expected non-collinear antiferromagnetic order was confirmed by the finding of weak zero-field magnetisation $\mathrm{(0.0086 \pm 0.0002) \mu_{B}/Mn}$ that does not saturate at high magnetic fields and has a Neel temperature of $\mathrm{(291 \pm 2)\, K}$.
